title: Read a dashboard: rows, tabs, and links

blocks.content: Explore two dashboards on Grafana Play to see how rows and tabs create meaningful sections, how a dashboard's layout and text help you understand it, and how links point you to the next useful view.
Explore the rows on Demo Wind Farm to see how rows group panels into meaningful sections, how collapsing a row hides its contents, and how the order of the rows forms a logical progression.
Open the **Demo Wind Farm** dashboard.

Focus on the **Wind Farm Power** row heading. This row groups a time series panel and a stat panel under one heading, making a meaningful section. A row can hold different types of panels. Its heading tells you what the panels cover before you read them.

Select the **Wind Farm Power** arrow to collapse the row. The row's panels are hidden. The heading stays visible so you can expand the row again. Collapsing and expanding rows lets you control what you see.
Select the **Wind Farm Power** arrow again to expand the row.
Find the row heading that starts with **Asset:**.
Take note that there are five panels using different formats.

Notice the **Alerts** row heading. This row holds one panel, an alert list. The three rows form a logical progression: from the wind farm as a whole, to a single asset, to alerts. The layout, where the panels sit and how large they are, follows that order from top to bottom. Panel size and position can help communicate the progression, but you need to read the panel content to understand it.
Explore Demo Wind Farm to see the text that introduces the dashboard's purpose, the link that helps you find the next useful view, and where a panel's description would go.

blocks.title: Introduction and links on Demo Wind Farm

blocks.content: Open the **Demo Wind Farm** dashboard.

Focus on the **Introduction** panel. This text panel near the top introduces the dashboard's purpose: what you can learn from it and where to start. It also names the data source. Helpful text like this gives you the context you need to understand the dashboard.

View the **Learn about Grafana through our Learning Journeys** link. A dashboard link is a shortcut at the top of a dashboard that takes you to another dashboard or an external website. This one goes to an external website, and its name explains what you will find there. Links help you choose where to go when you need more detail, and you can add them to your own dashboards.
Find the **Current Power** panel. Its title says what it shows, and it has no **i** icon, so it has no description.
Open the panel for editing.

blocks.content: Expand **Panel options** if it's collapsed.

blocks.content: Notice the **Description** field. It's empty. This is where a panel's description goes: what the value measures, why it matters, or how to read it alongside another panel. Once a panel has a description, you see it behind the small **i** icon in the top left corner of the panel. None of this dashboard's panels has one.
Explore the tabs on Time series graphs to see how a tab nests rows and shows one group's contents at a time.
Open the **Time series graphs** dashboard. If Grafana Play asks about unsaved changes even though you changed nothing, select **Discard**.

Notice the **Time Series Introduction** tab is selected. This tab contains rows, so the dashboard nests one grouping inside another. You can put rows inside a tab, rows inside a row, and tabs inside a row, up to four levels deep.
Select the **More Examples** tab. Each tab shows one group's contents at a time. Tabs let you break up a big dashboard or make one dashboard out of several smaller ones.
